integrity: The complete 1981 article was inspected around the original Burke–Shaw equations and attractor description. A same-object mathematical bibliographic record was checked for publication date, Burke–Shaw scope, and dynamical-systems MSC classification. An open 2022 review was checked for the exact general equations, standard parameter choices, and equilibria. A complete 2024 Burke–Shaw paper was searched for conditional, variance, moment, and invariant-measure formulations, with none found. Published semantic-index comparisons identified earlier global forcing balances as prior coverage; those integrated identities were removed from the originality claim. The three conditional regressions, variance defects, covariance identities, and first-defect equality classification were independently reconstructed and replayed with the packaged checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is conditional on compactly supported invariant probability measures and does not prove that such a measure exists for every positive parameter set.
The original d=13 Burke–Shaw example was described as noncompact and is not asserted to fall under the compact-support theorem.
The theorem does not determine the full invariant density, entropy, Lyapunov spectrum, fractal dimension, or basin geometry.

Historically earlier 1978 and 1981 sources were verified only without a day-resolved public date; the structured date uses the earliest checked day-resolved same-object mathematical source rather than inventing a day.
Previously published global forcing balances obtained after integrating some of the fiber laws are excluded from the originality claim.
A differently phrased equivalent conditional-moment observation could remain in unindexed literature.
title: Fiberwise stationary regressions in the Burke–Shaw flow
